questions.question: Which freedom fighter of British India is widely regarded as the 'father of the two-nation theory'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Syed Ahmed Khan.

  • Sir Syed Ahmed Khan was the founder of Aligarh Muslim University and a reformer.
  • He is widely regarded as the originator of the two-nation theory.
  • Muhammad Ali Jinnah later used this theory to demand Pakistan and became its first Governor-General (1947-48).

questions.question: Who among the following was a Roman Catholic missionary who worked in Bengal for the majority of his/her life?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mother Teresa.

  • Mother Teresa (from Macedonia) worked in Kolkata, Bengal for most of her life.
  • She won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979.
  • She founded the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata.

questions.question: When did Indigo revolt, a peasant movement, start in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1859 (March).

  • The Indigo Rebellion (Neel Bidroh) started in Bengal in March 1859.
  • It was a revolt by farmers against British planters who forced them to grow indigo under unfavorable terms.
  • The play 'Neel Darpan' by Dinabandhu Mitra depicted this oppression.

questions.question: The Paris Indian Society was an Indian nationalist organisation founded in
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1905.

  • The Paris Indian Society was founded in 1905 at Paris.
  • It was under the patronage of Madam Bhikaji Cama, Munchershah Burjori Godej, and S.R. Rana.
  • It was a branch of the Indian Home Rule Society established in London in 1905.
  • Bhikaji Cama's important publication is 'Vande Mataram' (1909).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Shyamji Krishna Verma and India House:
1. India House in London was established by Shyamji Krishna Verma in 1909.
2. He never founded the Indian Home Rule Society.
3. He became the first President of the Bombay Arya Samaj.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 3 only.

  • Statement 1 is incorrect: India House was established in 1905, not 1909.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: He did found the Indian Home Rule Society.
  • Statement 3 is correct: He became the first President of the Bombay Arya Samaj.
  • He also founded 'The Indian Sociologist' journal.

questions.question: Identify the freedom fighter who, as a child, hated going to school and found it suffocating and oppressive.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore.

  • Rabindranath Tagore hated going to school as a child and found it suffocating.
  • He founded Santiniketan (1901) and Visva-Bharati University (1921).
  • He won the Nobel Prize in Literature (1913) for 'Gitanjali'.
  • He composed 'Jana Gana Mana' (India's National Anthem) and 'Amar Shonar Bangla' (Bangladesh's National Anthem).

questions.question: The claim for 'swarajya' or self-government within the British Empire, on the model of self-governing colonies like Australia and Canada, was put forward from the Congress platform in 1905 by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

  • Gopal Krishna Gokhale was known as the 'Diamond of India'.
  • He was the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi.
  • He was Congress President in 1905.
  • He established the Servants of India Society (1905) and started 'The Hitavada' newspaper.
  • Mahatma Gandhi called him 'Dharmatma Gokhale'.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Bhoodan Yojana (Land Gift) movement:
1. The Bhoodan Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1931.
2. It was first started at Sevagram in Maharashtra.
3. The movement aimed to provide free education to rural children.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is None of the above.

  • Statement 1 is incorrect: The Bhoodan Movement was launched by Acharya Vinoba Bhave in 1951, not by Gandhi.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: It was first started at Pochampally village (Telangana), not Sevagram.
  • Statement 3 is incorrect: The movement aimed to persuade wealthy landowners to voluntarily give land to landless people, not provide education.

questions.question: The first President of the All India Trade Union Congress was
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lala Lajpat Rai.

  • AITUC was created on October 31, 1920 in Bombay.
  • It is the first Central Trade Union of India.
  • Lala Lajpat Rai was its first President.
  • Trade Unions in India are registered under the Trade Union Act (1926).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Dadabhai Naoroji:
1. He was the first Indian to become the Governor-General of India.
2. He was the first Indian to be selected to the British House of Commons on a Liberal Party ticket.
3. He was the founder of the Arya Samaj movement.
4. He was the first Indian to be appointed as the Vice-President of the Council of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2 only.

  • Statement 1 is incorrect: C. Rajagopalachari was the first Indian Governor-General, not Dadabhai Naoroji.
  • Statement 2 is correct: He was the first Indian elected to the British House of Commons on a Liberal Party ticket.
  • Statement 3 is incorrect: Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati.
  • Statement 4 is incorrect: He was not appointed as Vice-President of the Council of India.
  • He was known as 'India Gladstone' and coined the name 'Indian National Congress'.
  • He made the first attempt to calculate India's National Income.

questions.question: Who among the following Indian freedom fighters was fondly called Gandhi Buri (Old Lady Gandhi) for her dedication towards Gandhian principles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Matangini Hazra.

  • Matangini Hazra was an Indian revolutionary and social activist.
  • She was fondly called 'Gandhi Buri' (Old Lady Gandhi) for her dedication to Gandhian principles.
  • She participated actively in the Indian independence movement.

questions.question: Avadh Kisan Sabha was set up in the year
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1920.

  • Oudh Kisan Sabha (Avadh Farmers Association) was formed by Baba Ram Chandra in 1920.
  • He organized the farmers of Oudh and led the first protest against landlords.

questions.question: India and Pakistan had signed the ______ under which the two countries agreed to sort out differences and disputes bilaterally.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Shimla Pact.

  • The Shimla Pact was signed in 1972.
  • It was signed by Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto (President of Pakistan) and Indira Gandhi (Prime Minister of India).
  • Both countries agreed to sort out differences and disputes bilaterally.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the annexation of Hyderabad into India:
1. Operation Polo was the code name of the Hyderabad 'police action' launched in September 1948.
2. The princely state of Hyderabad voluntarily merged into the Indian Union without any military intervention.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 only.

  • Statement 1 is correct: Operation Polo was the code name for the Hyderabad police action in September 1948.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: Hyderabad did not voluntarily merge; the Indian Armed Forces invaded the Nizam-ruled state and annexed it.

questions.question: With whom is the 'Patharughat Uprising' associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Peasants' uprising.

  • The Patharughat Uprising was against the tax policies of the British in 1894.
  • Patharughat is a place in Assam (now known as Patharighat).
  • It was a peasants' uprising against oppressive British taxation.

questions.question: The movement ______ was led by Chaudhary Devi Lal in 1987.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nyaya Yudh.

  • Chaudhary Devi Lal led the 'Nyaya Yudh' (War for Justice) movement in 1987.
  • He founded the Lok Dal party.

questions.question: Chandernagore (Chandannagar) was a ______ colony captured by the British Navy on 23 March 1757.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is French.

  • Chandernagore (now Chandannagar) was a French colony.
  • The Battle of Chandernagore (1757) was fought between the French and British (led by Robert Clive).
  • It took place during the Seven Years' War (1756-1763).

questions.question: In which of the following years did Japan invade India resulting in the Battle of Imphal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1944.

  • Japan invaded India in 1944, resulting in the Battle of Imphal.
  • The outcome was a turning point of one of the most grueling campaigns of World War II (1939-45).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the reorganisation of Bombay State:
1. The Bombay Reorganisation Act was passed in 1960, leading to the division of Bombay State into Gujarat and Maharashtra.
2. The division of Bombay State under the Act was based on religious differences between Hindus and Muslims.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 only.

  • Statement 1 is correct: The Bombay Reorganisation Act was passed in 1960, dividing Bombay State into Gujarat and Maharashtra.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The division was based on linguistic lines (Gujarati-speaking and Marathi-speaking populations), not religious differences.

questions.question: Who among the following is one of the founder members of Bhartiya Jana Sangh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Shyama Prasad Mukherjee.

  • Bhartiya Jana Sangh (BJS) was an Indian right-wing political party that existed from 1951 to 1977.
  • It was the political arm of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS).
  • Shyama Prasad Mukherjee was one of its founder members.

questions.question: A large area of land demarcated as Damin-i-Koh in 1832 was declared as the land of the
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Santhals.

  • Damin-i-Koh was a large area of land demarcated in 1832.
  • It was declared as the land of the Santhals (tribals who inhabited the forests of Rajmahal hills).
  • The British promised non-interference in the land.

questions.question: Fort Saint Louis was a fort that stood in Pondicherry on the eastern coast of India. It belonged to the
questions.solution:
The correct answer is French.

  • Fort Saint Louis was a French fort in Pondicherry.
  • It was built by Francois Martin and destroyed by the British in 1761.

questions.question: What was the meaning of 'Ryot' in British records in the 18th century?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Peasants.

  • 'Ryot' meant peasants in British records.
  • Ryots were individual cultivators who had full rights regarding the sale, transfer, and leasing of land as long as they paid the rent.
  • This was under the Ryotwari system, where land revenue was paid by farmers directly to the state.

questions.question: Who was the Nawab of Bhopal that ruled from 1868 to 1901?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Shah Jahan Begum.

  • Nawabs of Bhopal:
    • Nawab Sikandar Begum: 1860-1868
    • Begum Sultan Shah Jahan: 1844-1860 and 1868-1901
    • Begum Kaikhusrau Jahan: 1901-1926
    • Begum Sajida Sultan: 1961-1995

questions.question: Who among the following was one of the speakers after Jawaharlal Nehru to address the Parliament on the midnight of 15 August 1947?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.

  • Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (first Vice President of India) was one of the three main speakers at the Central Hall of Parliament.
  • The other speakers were Jawaharlal Nehru (Tryst with Destiny speech) and Chaudhary Khaliquzaman.
